audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup is tagged diff FAV but carries diffRating 8/10, carryRating 8.5/10, a red tone token and prose reading 'Hard matchup' — four fields describing three different matchups.
audit.why: 52.19% over 502 games is a mild Mundo favourite that is lost early and won on items, not a hard counter.
audit.corrected: diffRating 6.5/10, carryRating 6.5/10, tone recoloured to the even token, and both prose ratings restated as 'Even matchup'.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[4..6] and phases[4..6].side all read 'Skill' while the prose on those exact rows says the opposite: whys[4] 'Level 6 still favours him', spikes[1] '6 is still his window not yours', whys[5] 'yours', whys[6] 'the late game is yours'. phases[4].why also promised the lane flips at 6.
audit.why: Heimerdinger's spike is UPGRADE!!! turrets, not a Mundo window; Mundo's spike is the HP/MR stack that lets him facetank the grid. That is exactly the packet levelChart.
audit.corrected: Level 6 -> Heimerdinger (4/10), First item -> Dr. Mundo, 2+ items -> Dr. Mundo (7/10), as one atomic group, with phases[4].why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fields claim Heimerdinger's grenade 'stops your E dash cold' / 'cancels your E dash'. Dr. Mundo's E, Blunt Force Trauma, has range 0 and is an auto-attack reset bag slam — he has no dash anywhere in his kit. The matchup's actual decisive interaction was never stated: Mundo's passive resists the FIRST immobilizing effect, so the CH-2 grenade stun is absorbed and drops a healing cannister.
audit.why: The focus ability of the whole page is that stun. Knowing it is eaten once — and that the second one is the real one — is the difference between diving the nest and dying in it.
audit.corrected: The dash claims are gone; the passive-eats-the-first-grenade interaction now appears in spikes[1], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].
